newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moderate earthquake strikes Japan near Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Moderate earthquake strikes Japan near Tokyo.

text.p: A moderately strong earthquake jolted the Izu Peninsula southwest of Tokyo on Wednesday night, Japan's Meteorological Agency said.

The quake occurred at 10:58 p.m. (1358 GMT) and registered 4.3 on the open-ended Richter scale. The strongest intensity was felt in the town of Ito, measuring 4 on the Japanese scale of up to 7, the agency said. In such a tremor, houses shake and unstable articles, such as tall vases, fall to the floor.
There were no immediate reports of damage from the quake.
The quake was the biggest in a series of more than 1,900 minor tremors since Tuesday night off the east coast of the Izu Peninsula, the officials said.
The area, a popular tourist destination 100 km (60 miles) from Tokyo, has long been an active seismic area with series of minor tremors striking for periods of up to a week.
Agency officials said seismic activity in this latest series of quakes was stronger than in July when some 315 minor quakes were registered.
